extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, and writers interested in the literary genre of magical realism
extracted.subtask_description: Understanding the salient characteristics and distinctions of the magical realism literary mode to guide reading or composition of works that blend realistic detail with magical elements. Covers typical techniques, narrative attitudes, and genre-distinctions used by critics and practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fantastical realism elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Magical realism portrays fantastical events in an otherwise realistic tone, bringing fables, folk tales, and myths into contemporary social relevance; fantasy traits (levitation, telepathy, telekinesis) appear to help encompass modern political realities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: use of levitation, telepathy, etc., as normalized traits; employ fantastical motifs to reflect or amplify social/political conditions rather than to build a separate fantasy system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-world setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers do not invent new worlds; magical elements are revealed within an existing, realistic or mundane setting. For characters, extraordinary events are treated as ordinary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: creating an alternate world or full secondary world (that would be fantasy). Example: Gabriel García Márquez's One Hundred Years of Solitude — supernatural occurrences happen within an everyday community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial reticence (matter-of-fact narration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberate withholding of information and explanations about the disconcerting fictitious world; the narrator is indifferent and presents supernatural events with logical precision as if nothing extraordinary happened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: avoid explaining the magical; present events calmly and without authorial astonishment so the reader accepts the marvelous as normal. Scoring/quality note: strong reticence increases the 'magic-realism' effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plenitude (baroque abundance of detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: A lack of emptiness; an extraordinary abundance of disorienting, associative detail (a layering of elements) that contributes to a sense of the marvelous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rich, layered description and associative imagery rather than sparse minimalism. Carpentier's notion of the baroque/plenitude is cited as characteristic of Latin American 'boom' novels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybridity (multiple, coexisting planes of reality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot lines characteristically employ hybrid multiple planes of reality that exist in inharmonious arenas (e.g., urban/rural, Western/indigenous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: juxtapose conflicting worldviews or social spheres so that different 'realities' coexist without reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metafiction / textualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on the reader's role, the interplay of fiction and reality, story-within-a-story effects, and cases where a textual world enters the reader's real world or a fictitious reader appears in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use self-reflexive devices (textualization) to blur boundaries between fiction and reality; useful for drawing attention to social or political criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heightened awareness of mystery
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaving out explanation or obfuscating elements to create confusion and a sense of mystery; readers must let go of conventional exposition, linear time, and scientific reason to perceive connectedness or hidden meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: omit conventional causal exposition, allow ambiguity, encourage readers to seek symbolic or layered meaning rather than tidy explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political critique and subversive function
rubrics_metrics.description: Magic realism often contains implicit criticism of society and elites and functions as a mode for marginalized perspectives; its 'alternative world' corrects or contests established viewpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use magical elements to expose or reframe social and political injustices; this subversive dimension is especially emphasized in Latin American magic-realism criticism (decentering hegemonic discourse).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing history and fantasy
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration of historical events or contexts with fantastical elements to comment on reality (e.g., telepathic children born at a nation's independence), using mythic/fantastic devices to reinterpret history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: place magical elements in direct relation to historical turning points or collective memory to create political or cultural allegory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matter-of-factness (ontological acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative treats inexplicable events as ordinary fact; the supernatural is integrated into the world-view of characters and narration rather than being treated as anomalous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct from authorial reticence only in emphasis: matter-of-factness concerns how the fictional community accepts magic; aim to write scenes where characters' daily responses normalize the marvelous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction from fantasy (integration vs problematization of the supernatural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike fantasy where the supernatural is a separate problematic code, in magical realism the supernatural is accepted and presented as part of reality; fantasy often draws special attention to the otherworldly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: foregrounding elaborate systems of magic, explanatory worldbuilding, or treating miracles as mysteries to be solved — these tend to push a text toward fantasy rather than magical realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction from surrealism (material vs psychological emphasis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Surrealism focuses on the unconscious, dreams, and psychological interiority; magical realism emphasizes the material/actual existence of magical phenomena within the social world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If magical events function primarily as dreamlike expressions of inner psychology, the work aligns with surrealism; to be magical-realist, present magic as a tangible part of the external world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction from fabulism (use of specific myths vs generalized magic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabulism incorporates specific myths, fairy tales, or parables and often serves explicit allegory; magical realism more commonly uses general magical elements and is culturally or politically situated (traditionally linked to Latin America).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your work explicitly reuses or reworks well-known myths as allegory, it may be fabulism; magical realism usually integrates magic into everyday life without relying solely on canonical mythic plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to realism (use realism as framework to extend reality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Magical realism relies upon the presentation of realistic detail and objective narration so that the fantastic can stretch what is acceptable as real without violating manifest coherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: ground the story in careful, concrete realist detail (settings, social conditions, character routines) so that the introduction of magic feels consequential rather than arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spindler's typology (three kinds of magic realism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ceylan Spindler (Guatemala) suggests three types: 'metaphysical' (estrangement/uncanny), 'ontological' (matter-of-fact relating of inexplicable events), and 'anthropological' (Native worldview juxtaposed with Western rationality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the typology as an analytic tool or compositional choice: decide whether your emphasis is estrangement, matter-of-factness, or the juxtaposition of cultural epistemologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lo real maravilloso (marvelous realism) vs magical realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Carpentier's 'lo real maravilloso' frames a heightened reality where the marvelous seems natural because of the region's history and culture; he contrasts a unidimensional 'marvelous' world (where anything can happen) with the bidimensional world of magical realism (supernatural blends with the familiar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compositional implication: if the entire fictional universe is saturated with the supernatural (one-dimensional marvelous), readers perceive a different mode than when magic intrudes into an otherwise realist world (bidimensional magical realism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience/readership expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Magical realist works often aim at a sophisticated readership attuned to textual subtleties, intertextuality, and political/postcolonial resonance rather than mass-market escapism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider reader expectations when choosing complexity of structure, levels of ambiguity, and the degree of overt entertainment vs intellectual subtlety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative devices typical of the mode (textualization, story-within-story, non-linear time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques commonly used include textualization (reader enters story or story enters reader's world), metafictional devices, non-linear chronology, and open-ended/expansive romanticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ structural devices (nested stories, jumps in time, unreliable chronologies) to harmonize with magical elements and to foreground thematic or political concerns.
